'''''Aria edulis''''', the '''whitebeam''' or '''common whitebeam''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is a species of [[deciduous]] tree in the family ''[[Rosaceae]]''.

The tree often forms new shoots around the trunk. Typically compact and domed, the plant has a few upswept branches and the leaves have an almost-white underside. The [[plant sexuality|hermaphrodite]] cream-white flowers appear in May, are insect pollinated, and go on to produce scarlet berries, which are often eaten by birds.<ref>The [[Reader's Digest]] Field Guide to the Trees and Shrubs of Britain ''p.86''.</ref>

It is native to most of Europe as well as North Africa (Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia) and temperate Asia ([[Eastern Anatolia Region|Eastern]] [[Turkey]], Armenia, Georgia).<ref name="GRIN">{{GRIN}}</ref> It generally favours dry limestone and chalk soils.

The [[cultivars]] ''A. edulis'' 'Lutescens',<ref>{{cite web |title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Sorbus aria'' 'Lutescens' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/17534/Sorbus-aria-Lutescens/Details |access-date=5 March 2021}}</ref> with very whitish-green early leaves, and ''A. edulis'' 'Majestica',<ref>{{cite web |title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Sorbus aria'' 'Majestica' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/90459/Sorbus-aria-Majestica/Details |access-date=5 March 2021}}</ref> with large leaves, have both gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |title=AGM Plants - Ornamental |date=July 2017 |page=98 |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=13 November 2018}}</ref>

The berries are edible when overripe ([[Bletting|bletted]]).<ref>{{cite book |last=Mabey |first=Richard |title=Food for Free |publisher=Collins |year=2012 |isbn=978-000-743847-1 |location=London |page=72 |author-link=Richard Mabey}}</ref>
